A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MC-Bench and contain readable main texts, figures, tables and complete appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, diagnostic experiments and evaluations by three human volunteers on MC-Bench.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds finetuning results, a training-data ablation and individual human-evaluation scores.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a Qwen2-VL-7B adaptation procedure using LoRA and a mixture of collected image-level instruction data and synthesized paired-image localization data. This is a substantive new training approach. The earlier GPT-4o/G-DINO stepwise pipeline remains procedurally unchanged under the name agentic baseline.

E1.justification: v2 adds training coverage encompassing multi-image comparison/captioning and VQA from Birds-to-Words and Multi-VQA, plus synthetic paired-image localization derived from LVIS and OmniLabel. v1 contains no corresponding training corpus. MC-Bench's evaluation domains, three prompt styles and 20 skills remain substantially unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds InternVL2.5-8B with both sequence and merged-image inputs, along with the new finetuned Qwen2-VL-7B baseline. The previous comparator set is retained; CogVLM-G becomes CogVLM-Grounding, and the stepwise baseline becomes the agentic baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds a finetuning protocol using approximately 60K samples over three epochs, with separate image-level, instance-level and mixed-data training conditions compared against unfinetuned models. The reported benchmark composition also changes from 1,709 positive/291 negative samples and 3,202 boxes to 1,712/288 and 3,200 boxes. The 2,000-sample evaluation-only design and Acc/AP50 metrics remain.

E4.justification: Appendix C and Figure 9 add a focused ablation testing whether image-level data, synthetic instance-level data or their mixture benefits finetuning. Existing model-size, grouping, prediction-count, object-size and negative-input analyses remain, with expanded model coverage. The two pipeline failure cases are retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions use three human evaluators and report their average performance. v2 adds individual point scores in Table 9, but introduces no uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-training seed/run reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises many scores: sequence Qwen2-VL-72B AP50 changes from 31.9 to 30.7, and human AP50 from 43.1 to 41.3. It adds InternVL2.5 results and a finetuned baseline scoring 57.7 Acc/22.6 AP50. Figure 9 adds data-mixture findings, but its unfinetuned 7B AP50 is approximately 20.2 versus 19.1 in Table 2. Revised annotation counts also limit direct cross-version performance interpretation.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The task definitions and maximum-mean-IoU group-matching criterion remain unchanged; v2's identification of the Hungarian algorithm adds implementation specificity rather than new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add the finetuned baseline as a contribution, and the results claim benefits from multi-context instruction tuning. The central contributions remain the proposed grounding task, MC-Bench and the substantial model–human performance gap.

C2.justification: v2 conjectures that detection-derived synthetic training data mainly teaches referring while providing limited comparison and reasoning capabilities. It also adds an interpretation of the agentic baseline's small-object advantage and expands downstream applicability discussion. Existing limitations concerning two-image inputs, incomplete skill coverage and human variability are retained or relocated.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands documentation through an annotation JSON schema/API description, explicit GPT-4o, Gemini and Qwen2-VL prompts, and the finetuning data-generation recipe, framework and hyperparameters. It specifies Hungarian matching, qualifies the earlier four-RTX-3090 hardware statement with a Qwen2-VL-72B exception, and announces an MC-Bench v0.5 release.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands cited research across grounding, multimodal models, applications and training methods. Section 2 explicitly acknowledges concurrent multi-image approaches Migician, CALICO and PRIMA; Table 1 adds OmniLabel. New training-related references include LoRA and LLaMA-Factory. These additions extend beyond bibliographic updates to retained works.

P1.justification: Much of the original prose and main section sequence remains. v2 rewrites the abstract to feature finetuning, polishes terminology, reorders related-work subsections, expands appendix organization and moves references after the appendices. The stepwise-to-agentic renaming is primarily editorial.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive figure and table resizing and relocation. Figure 4 gains a nested sample-distribution chart; Figure 3 revises examples and labels. New displays include application examples, the training ablation, annotation schema, model prompts and individual human results. The original analysis and failure-case figures are retained under new numbers.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, explicit grounding prompts, the annotation schema and training recipe improve reproducibility, while the finetuning experiment and data-mixture ablation provide useful additional evidence. These benefits are tempered by unexplained annotation/score revisions and unreconciled Figure 9/Table 2 values, which limit confidence in the new quantitative evidence.
